Decision: Raised at the first re-attestation sitting: the generated pending projection was a POINTER where the owner needed the before/after, and the depth that makes a re-attest readable is a word-level diff, which markdown cannot express. Title: concurrency-v2 B2: strike or restate the specs-mirror-the-terminal-folders sentence
OneLine: RULED 2026-08-01: RESTATE (a) - executed the same date (B2 amended in place; the archive stays flat by decision; declared-absences lines restated). Original brief: rule whether concurrency-v2 B2's second sentence is STRUCK or RESTATED - a decision about the DESIGN TEXT only; WI-391, the row that would have built it, is already cancelled under either answer
Decision: SCOPE FIRST, because it is easy to misread: this rules on the SENTENCE, not on whether anything gets built. B2 says a closed WI's spec-of-record moves to docs/archive/specs/complete/ or docs/archive/specs/cancelled/ rather than one flat docs/archive/specs/, so a spec's location answers shipped-or-cancelled without opening it. WI-391 was filed to build that and instead refuted it on measurement; the refutation was independently confirmed (APPROVE findings=6, 2a4c9642). WI-391 is CANCELLED, not parked, because under BOTH options below its work does not happen - so a ruler here is choosing what the design record should SAY, with the build question already closed. The measurement, which either option must live with: the spec-to-folder mapping is not total (of 111 archived specs, 92 resolve to complete, 3 to cancelled, and 16 to nothing - 15 shared effort docs plus WI-300-sr052-binding.2026-07-26.md, whose name does not match _own_spec's own glob); it is contradictory for at least one file (research-knowledge.2026-07-29.md is cited from both terminal states, and R-F archives a shared doc when its LAST open citer closes, so both folders are correct for it); there is no regenerator to gate the derived location for freshness (gen_trajectory.py names 'archive' zero times); for the 92 attributable specs docs/work/ already answers shipped-or-cancelled by location; and no reader consumes the split - every one of them would have to widen its glob to ignore it. ON THE TIMING, so the record is not read as a criticism of the filing: WI-391 was correctly filed given the ruling it inherited, and refutation is exactly what a claimed row is for. The available improvement is only about WHERE the question gets asked. The intake said AT FILING, in its own words, that the row 'deletes no machinery, closes no raise path and makes no bad state unrepresentable' and 'must justify itself on the navigation benefit alone' - and section 0 prescribes asking 'what constraint would make this unrepresentable?' at FILING, where the cost is still comparable. Applied then, the answer was already 'none, by the row's own admission'. So this is the process working, one step later than section 0 prescribes.
BlastRadius: One sentence in docs/concurrency-v2.md B2, and the two docs/declared-absences entries that name the destinations and now point at this item. Nothing in docs/archive/specs/ moves under either option, so no link migration is incurred and no downstream repo is affected. Note one measured trap for whoever executes the ruling: the two declared-absences lines must be RESTATED, never deleted - deleting them adds +2 dangling references under check_doc_refs --strict, because the cancelled WI-391 spec's own title names both paths and stays in the registry permanently.
Options: (a) RESTATE - amend the sentence to record what the measurement found: the goal is met by the registry half for every attributable spec, and is unmeetable by any folder layout for the 16 that are not. FOR: the sentence's GOAL is sound and only its LOCATION is wrong, so restating preserves a correct intent while correcting a wrong mechanism; it leaves the 16 undecidable files named in the design record, which is the durable fact a future reader needs, since a flat docs/archive/specs/ will keep inviting the same tidy-up; and B2's own readers meet the correction where they meet the claim. AGAINST: it leaves a sentence that reads as a partial retreat rather than a clean decision, and it keeps text in a design doc describing something the repo deliberately does not do, which is its own kind of clutter. (b) STRIKE - delete the sentence outright. FOR: the kit's own state-it-once-and-link principle argues for deletion - the reasoning already has two homes (this item and the log fragment), so restating puts a third copy in the design doc; a design doc should describe the design, and this is no longer part of it; and a struck sentence cannot be misread later as a pending obligation, which a restated one can. AGAINST: B2's own readers then see no trace of the question, so the reasoning survives only where they are not looking - the tidy-up gets re-proposed by the next person to read a flat docs/archive/specs/, which is precisely how WI-391 came to be filed. (The claim that striking leaves 'no record of why' would be false - this item and the log fragment are that record - and the objection is narrower than that: it is about where the record is REACHABLE FROM.) (c) BUILD IT ANYWAY - accept a hand-adjudicated placement for the 16. FOR: B2 ships as written, and the navigation gain is real for anyone browsing the archive directly. AGAINST: it asserts a terminal state the repo does not hold for 14% of the corpus, has no honest answer at all for research-knowledge.2026-07-29.md, creates a second uncross-checked home for a fact the registry already carries, and adds a decision with a wrong-answer mode to every future close.
Recommendation: RESTATE (a). The goal in B2 is sound and is already achieved - a spec's shipped-or-cancelled IS answerable by location, at docs/work/ rather than at docs/archive/specs/ - so the sentence is wrong only in WHERE it puts the answer, and correcting it in place is a smaller and more honest edit than deleting it. The deciding argument against (b) is reachability rather than record-keeping: the 16 undecidable files do not go away, so a reader of a flat docs/archive/specs/ will reach for this tidy-up again, and B2 is where they will be reading. Weighed honestly, (b)'s state-it-once argument is the strongest case against this recommendation and a ruler may reasonably prefer it; the disagreement is narrow, and either way WI-391 stays cancelled.

Title: One machine-parseable carrier for the requirement registries - rule the .md + .csv split
OneLine: rule whether the four requirement tiers share ONE machine-parseable carrier - today SN is markdown prose and SR/LLR/TC are CSV, a split with no recorded rationale anywhere; recommendation is (b) one TOML carrier as the destination, sequenced as its own program after the repo is locked
Decision: RULED (owner, 2026-08-10): ONE TOML CARRIER, option (b), and brought FORWARD of the P0 sitting at the owner's direction so the new format is the one the remaining schema work lands on. Shape: id-keyed bare tables ([requirement.SR-137]), typed ref arrays, int Phase, multi-line strings for prose. Carrier only - Status keeps Draft/Verified/Modified, because retiring `Modified` is the ladder's job and doing it here would launder the 38 rows' re-blessing (Q11). See repo-lock D-5 for the guardrails.
BlastRadius: MEASURED, and it differs sharply by option. Reading 32 SN rows costs about 166 code lines across 14 functions in 8 modules; reading all 436 SR+LLR+TC rows PLUS every off-spine registry costs `trace.load_csv`, five lines, because `csv.DictReader` does the rest - so the SN tier costs roughly 28x the parsing code for 7 percent of the rows, and it is also the only tier with no schema tier at all (no required-field checks, no enum checks - reference doc section 12.5). Two of those SN readers are F5 twins pinned equal by `tests/test_rule_sync.py`; a third pair, `traj_parse._sn_rows` and `gen_okf.sn_rows`, is pinned by nothing but a docstring saying -change both together- and HAS ALREADY DRIFTED ONCE, rendering a phantom SN-000 root in the dashboard icicle - a live hazard under every option, including keeping things as they are. Option (b) is a kit version bump with a downstream migration: every F5-duplicated loader, the shipped templates, `bootstrap.py` MAPPING, `EXAMPLE.md`, `ADOPTING.md`, `registry-machinery-reference.md` and the OKF export; `trace.structure_findings` (column-count integrity) has no analogue, though a parse error is arguably a stronger check; and `test_dogfood_sync`'s ordered-superset header rule has no meaning over TOML keys and needs redesigning. The precedent is IN-REPO and its cost is known rather than estimated: `work-items.csv` already became the `docs/work/` TOML-frontmatter spec folder, as a multi-phase program (2b, the 2c authority flip, Phase 5's deletion of the CSV home) spanning weeks, forcing a re-attestation sitting (LLR-051/056 re-grounded, SR-129/LLR-136 flipped Modified) and surfacing real defects - `build_scope_srs` and `critique_control` had been reading silently EMPTY since the 2c flip, which is the fail-open shape this kit exists to catch. A spine migration is LARGER than that one, because the WI registry carries no upward or downward joins into three sibling registries and the spine does. CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (the owner refuted the earlier wording, and this cell carried it): the FIELDS are carrier-neutral - `TextHash` and `HashedOn` (renamed from `TextDigest` / `AcceptedCommit`) are fields, not a format - but the CODE AND TESTS ARE NOT, so deferring this ruling does NOT cost nothing. Building the anchor on CSV and converting afterwards rewrites the column-classification machinery, test_dogfood_sync's ordered-superset header rule (meaningless over TOML keys), structure_findings (a column count becomes a parse error), intake's writer, the two-tree git-show parse, and the attestation test module a SECOND time. Forecloses-nothing is true of the design and false of the labour; see repo-lock.md F-7. This ruling now GATES the anchor half of D-1, D-2, and the D-3/D-4 registry changes.
Options: (a) KEEP THE SPLIT and ratify it as a decision, recording the rationale that was never written. FOR: zero cost and zero risk; the CSV tiers are read by five lines of stdlib and they work; a lock program exists to CLOSE the largest amendment window this repo has carried, and this would open a larger one on top of it. AGAINST: it ratifies an accident rather than a design; it leaves the 166-line SN reader and the unpinned `traj_parse`/`gen_okf` twin standing; and it leaves the SN tier - the one a G1 consistency review leans on hardest - with no schema tier at all. (b) ONE TOML CARRIER for all four tiers. FOR: `tomllib` is stdlib at the kit's declared 3.11 floor, so it costs no dependency - unlike a markdown parser, which `docs/dependencies.md` would have to admit as the first Python row ever, in the shipped tier the kit holds stdlib-preferred; the kit ALREADY sanctions TOML in two homes (`docs/process.toml` and the +++ frontmatter of every `docs/work` spec); multi-line basic strings dissolve every measured carrier defect at once; typed arrays retire `refs()` splitting on whitespace and with it the SN-001-and-SN-002 orphan bug (reference doc section 12.8); TOML carries COMMENTS, which CSV cannot - today the SR template fakes them by stuffing a 700-character explanation of the Phase rule inside an example row's cell value; and it unifies SN with the other three tiers behind one loader, deleting about 139 lines of bespoke parsing. AGAINST: `tomllib` is READ-ONLY (PEP 680 omitted a writer deliberately) and this kit writes registries programmatically - `intake` rewrites Status today and must write the anchor cells under D-1 - so it needs a third hand-rolled emitter or the first genuinely shared one; the repo already carries two, by two strategies that are NOT interchangeable (`wi_convert.toml_string` re-serializes and re-parses to verify; `bootstrap.set_process_key` does a line rewrite so the explanatory header survives, which works only because that file owes the git hooks one key per line); plus the kit version bump and downstream migration sized above. (c) MARKDOWN TABLES EVERYWHERE, for consistency with SN. FOR: one carrier, and the most directly readable in an editor. AGAINST: REFUTED ON MEASUREMENT - five live cells already contain a literal pipe character (SR-024, SR-043, LLR-024, LLR-040, LLR-152), which `traj_parse`'s naive split-on-pipe shape cannot survive; 552 cells contain commas, which CSV handles by RFC-4180 quoting and markdown has no equivalent for; the longest cell is 1553 characters; an embedded newline has no representation at all (none exist today, but the CSV form permits one and `gen_open_items.normalize` exists because a Windows-authored multi-line cell was observed); there is no analogue for `trace.structure_findings`; and there is no reusable markdown-table reader here to inherit - the `docs/work` loader parses no tables at all (it is `tomllib` over +++ fences, small BECAUSE the fields are TOML) and the SN tables are read by six bespoke scanners, two of which index cells POSITIONALLY, which is exactly the failure the column-count guard exists to catch.
Recommendation: (b) as the DESTINATION, (a) as the ACTION for this program - and those are not in conflict. The carrier question has a right answer and it is TOML: it is the only option that is stdlib at the declared floor, already sanctioned in two homes here, and able to hold the cells that actually exist rather than the cells one wishes existed. But the lock program's whole purpose is to close an open amendment window, and a kit-wide carrier migration inside it would open a bigger one - so rule the destination now if you are ready, and sequence the work as its own program once the repo is locked. IF (b) IS RULED: it graduates to an SN plus its SR on the SN-011 shape - a constraint recorded as a need, which is already what this kit does with stack-agnosticism and the dependency floor - and the F-8 gap, that a design constraint has no declared home at all, becomes worth its own row rather than a note. IF (a) IS RULED: record the rationale in `PROCESS.md` so the next reader does not re-derive it from scratch, as this one did. EITHER WAY, one thing is owed separately and should not wait on this ruling: the `traj_parse._sn_rows` / `gen_okf.sn_rows` twin is pinned by no test and has already drifted once, and that hazard is identical under all three options.

Title: What does Status MEAN - align the vocabulary across all six registries, including the interfaces pair
OneLine: rule what `Status` means across the six registries that carry one - the word names six different vocabularies today, one of them (`interfaces.csv`) undeclared, self-overlapping, read by nothing mechanical, and fed verbatim to LLM planning briefs; recommendation is to reserve `Status` for ratifiable-artifact maturity and rename the rest, executed WITH OI-12 because both rewrite registry definitions
Decision: Raised by the owner 2026-08-09 while ruling on whether a stakeholder need should gain a `Status` cell: -we need to align on all the registry definitions. I am afraid this will impact the interface definitions as well.- Verified, and it does. SIX CARRIERS TODAY, only one of them closed: (1) SR/LLR/TC `Status` - OPEN vocabulary with three magic values (`Draft`, `Verified`, `Modified`) matched by exact equality, case-insensitive, everything else legal and mechanically inert; (2) SN - NO column at all, maturity is section-as-state, a heading whose text CONTAINS the word draft, so the SN rule is a substring match where the row rule is an equality; (3) WI - directory-as-state, seven directories mapping to eight in-memory names (`complete/` becomes `done`) with `blocked` DERIVED and never stored - the only CLOSED vocabulary in the repo, because an unknown directory is a loader refusal; (4) IF `Status` - {Stable, Active, Draft}; (5) OI `Status` - only `pending` carries meaning; (6) CMP `State`. THE INTERFACES REGISTRY IS THE WORST OF THE SIX AND IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE: `PROCESS.md` section 8 names the IF row's fields as -direction, counterpart, contract, the SR-Refs that realize/rely on it, version, and stability- and `Status` IS NOT AMONG THEM, yet it ships in the template and carries a value on all 95 live rows (Stable 87, Active 4, Draft 4); it OVERLAPS its own neighbour, since `Stability` is {Stable, Experimental} and the word Stable appears in both columns of the same row meaning different things; and their enforcement is inverted from what a reader would assume - `Stability`, the DECLARED field, is read by exactly one consumer (`gen_release_checklist`), while `Status`, the UNDECLARED one, is read by nothing mechanical at all and its only consumer is `plan_briefs.IF_SURFACE_COLUMNS`, which hands it verbatim into the dual-plan LLM briefs. An undeclared, unvalidated, self-overlapping column is being presented to a model as fact. RULED 2026-08-11 (D-9): option (b), unify - Status means ONE thing repo-wide, a three-rung ladder Drafted -> Approved -> Founded, uniform across SN/SR/LLR/TC. Approved is defined generally as "a judgement was made", so it travels to other registries where the meaning stays coherent. The pass rung is DELETED rather than renamed: pass/fail is a live fact the harness answers, so recording it per row is a stale duplicate - and deleting it means Verified leaves the vocabulary entirely, so a stray Verified is unambiguously an un-migrated row. IF Status lands with OI-14; OI/CMP/WI dispositions in D-9 consequence 5. Migration is held behind the P0 sitting per Q11 (the 38 Modified rows must resolve first or their owed re-blessing is laundered).
BlastRadius: REGISTRY DEFINITIONS AND TEMPLATES, which is why this is coupled to OI-12 rather than independent of it. Any answer touches `docs/requirements/interfaces.csv` plus its shipped template, `PROCESS.md` section 8's field list, and - if the SN half is included - `stakeholder-needs.md`, its template, and the section-as-state readers in `trace.py` and `derive_gate.py` (F5 twins pinned by `tests/test_rule_sync.py`). A RENAME additionally touches every reader of the renamed column and every adopting repo, which is the same blast radius OI-12 carries, for the same files. NOTE THE SHARP EDGE ON THE SN HALF: giving an SN a `Status` cell while the section-as-state rule still stands is TWO HOMES FOR ONE DIAL, precisely the state SN-028 just shipped a REFUSAL for - so the cell and the retirement of section-as-state must land in ONE commit, never both live at once. What this does NOT touch: the gate arithmetic. `derive_gate` reads the three magic spine values and the SN section-state; nothing here proposes changing what they MEAN, only what the word is allowed to name elsewhere. Also independent of the carrier question in one direction only - the vocabulary survives any carrier, but executing a rename twice (once on CSV, once after a TOML conversion) is the same double-labour trap OI-12's own sequencing note records.
Options: (a) DECLARE, DO NOT UNIFY - leave each registry its own vocabulary and write down what each one means, adding a schema check where the vocabulary is meant to be closed. FOR: smallest possible change; the vocabularies genuinely describe different things, and a requirement's maturity is not an interface's stability, so forcing one word onto both would be a false unification; it fixes the actual defect (undeclared, unvalidated) without a rename. AGAINST: it leaves one word naming six things, which is the condition that produced the `interfaces.csv` overlap in the first place, and leaves a reader (or an agent) to infer from context which vocabulary a `Status` cell is speaking. (b) RESERVE THE WORD - `Status` means maturity-of-a-ratifiable-artifact and nothing else (the spine tiers, plus SN if that half is taken); everything else is RENAMED to what it actually is - the IF column collapses into `Stability` or becomes `Lifecycle`, OI becomes `Decision` state, CMP stays `State`. FOR: one word, one meaning, which is the kit's own single-source doctrine applied to a vocabulary rather than to a file; it makes the six-way ambiguity unrepresentable instead of documented; and it removes the undeclared IF column rather than blessing it. AGAINST: a rename across registries, templates, readers and every adopting repo - a kit version bump with a migration, and one that is pure churn if the value it carries is never read. (c) SN HALF ONLY - add the SN `Status` cell (with section-as-state retired in the same commit) and leave the other five alone. FOR: it unblocks D-2 and puts the five Draft needs onto the owner surface, which is the concrete thing anyone is waiting for. AGAINST: it makes the ambiguity WORSE by adding a sixth `Status` while the interfaces defect stands, and it is the option most likely to be described later as -we knew and did nothing-.
Recommendation: (b) as the destination, and EXECUTE IT WITH OI-12, not before or after. The coupling is the whole point: both items rewrite registry definitions, both touch every template, and both force a downstream migration - so doing them separately pays that cost twice, which is the same double-labour objection that reordered OI-12's own plan. If OI-12 rules TOML, the vocabulary lands as typed keys in the new carrier and the rename is absorbed by a migration that was happening anyway. TWO THINGS SHOULD NOT WAIT FOR EITHER RULING, because they are defects rather than design questions. FIRST, the `interfaces.csv` `Status` column: it is undeclared in `PROCESS.md` section 8, overlaps `Stability` in the same row, is read by nothing mechanical, and is fed verbatim to LLM planning briefs - that last fact is what makes it urgent rather than untidy, because a model is being handed an unvalidated field as though it were a contract. Either declare it with a distinct meaning or delete it and keep the field section 8 actually names. SECOND, the SN half is genuinely blocking D-2 and the owner surface; if the sitting wants the five Draft needs visible before this is ruled, take (c) KNOWINGLY, record it here as an accepted interim, and let (b) absorb it - what must not happen is (c) arriving by default and being mistaken for a decision.

Title: What is an IF row's Contract cell FOR - declare the interface registry's content contract
OneLine: rule what the `Contract` cell must contain, may contain, and must not - measured over all 95 live rows it carries design narrative and history rather than a pinned specification (1 percent requirement voice, 13 percent a callable signature, 27 percent a WI id), and nothing validates any of it because `--strict-schema` covers SR/LLR/TC only; recommendation is DECLARE now and SPLIT gradually, never a 95-row rewrite
Decision: Raised by the owner 2026-08-09 while reviewing the registries: -the prose in IF appear to be requirements, when it is intended to be interface definitions.- MEASURED OVER ALL 95 LIVE ROWS, and the reading holds with one correction. They are NOT requirements in the shall-statement sense - exactly one row uses shall or must - and section 8's backing rule holds mechanically, since ZERO rows have an empty `SR-Refs`, so every seam does hang off a real requirement. What the cells actually carry is DESIGN NARRATIVE: what a module does across the seam, which WI split it from what, and which defect the shape was chosen to avoid. 27 percent name a `WI-###`, 14 percent cite another registry id, 11 percent carry a rationale connective, 9 percent narrate a past incident, and only 13 percent name a callable signature. Median 260 characters, mean 323, max 968, with 21 rows over 500; in the five longest cells the history and incident sentences outnumber everything else. THE CONTENT IS NOT MISJUDGED, IT IS UNFILED - and the reason is structural rather than careless: the kit is stack-agnostic so a type signature cannot be demanded (a seam may be a file format, a CLI, or an external actor), and the IF row has NO `Rationale` and NO `Detail` column, so the why has nowhere else in the row to go. Someone had a true and useful thing to say and one cell to say it in.
BlastRadius: THE WHOLE IF REGISTRY HAS NO SCHEMA TIER. `trace.py`'s `--strict-schema` covers SR, LLR and TC only, so on an IF row nothing is required, nothing is enum-checked, and nothing bounds a cell's content - `Contract` is unconstrained, `Status` is undeclared (OI-13), and `Stability` is validated nowhere despite being the field `PROCESS.md` section 8 actually names. Ruling this therefore means adding a schema tier, not just writing prose. THREE CONSUMERS FEEL IT. (1) `plan_briefs.IF_SURFACE_COLUMNS` feeds `Contract` VERBATIM into the dual-plan LLM planning briefs, so history sentences spend brief budget without constraining behaviour and narrative sits mixed with normative statement in a prompt - the sharpest practical cost, and the one that argues for a split rather than a declaration alone. (2) A consuming row -pins the version- per section 8, but nothing in the cell marks which sentence is the pinned obligation, so a `Version` bump is measured against an unstated baseline. (3) 27 percent of cells name a `WI-###`, duplicating `log.md`; a WI id ages, and a cancelled row's id sitting in a `Contract` cell still reads as authority. AND ONE COUPLING A RULER SHOULD KNOW BEFORE DECIDING: how many IF rows this repo needs is not a free choice - `check_trajectory.cross_component_findings` (WI-064) makes an import edge between two components a finding unless a covering IF row exists, so the CMP partition DETERMINES the IF population. Ruling IF's content contract while the component model is unsettled rules half a question; the two should at least be read together.
Options: (a) DECLARE, LEAVE THE ROWS - write down in `PROCESS.md` section 8 and the shipped template what a `Contract` cell must contain, and give IF a schema tier (required fields, the closed `Stability` vocabulary). FOR: cheapest by far; it fixes the actual defect, which is that nothing SAYS what the cell is for, without touching 95 cells of prose that a maintainer wrote for a reason; new and amended rows land correct immediately. AGAINST: the 95 existing cells stay mixed, so the LLM-brief dilution and the unstated-pin problem both survive the ruling; a declaration nothing enforces retroactively is the weakest form of a rule. (b) SPLIT THE CELL - `Contract` keeps the binding specification; a new `Rationale` column takes the why; history is removed from the cells and lives in `log.md`, where it already does. FOR: it puts each kind of content in a home that exists for it, gives the LLM brief a cell worth quoting verbatim, and makes -what am I pinning- answerable. AGAINST: it is a schema change on a shipped registry (template, every adopter, `IF_SURFACE_COLUMNS`, the arch-graph render), and done as a SWEEP it is 95 prose rewrites with a real chance of quietly losing load-bearing maintainer knowledge - the `WI-218` facts are useful, just misfiled. (c) RULE IT FREE-FORM PROSE - accept that `Contract` is a description, say so in section 8, and stop implying a specification: stop feeding it to planning briefs as authority, and drop the -pins the version- language it cannot support. FOR: honest; it ends a claim the registry has never met, which is the one thing that is definitely wrong today. AGAINST: it gives up the seam registry's whole point - an interface nobody can pin is a comment - and it would be the first place this kit answers -we imply a check nobody performs- by lowering the claim rather than building the check.
Recommendation: (a) AS THE IMMEDIATE ACT, (b) AS THE DIRECTION, executed PER ROW AS ROWS ARE TOUCHED rather than as a sweep. Declaring costs almost nothing and fixes the root defect - the cell has never had a stated purpose, so no one has been writing it wrongly, only differently. Add the schema tier in the same pass, because `Stability` being enum-checked and `Contract` being required are the two rules the registry can enforce today without any prose migration. Then let the split arrive with normal work: a row whose seam is edited gets its history moved to the log and its why moved to the new column, so the corpus converges without a 95-row commit nobody can review carefully.
